answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity's standing is its cumulative record of completed, independently verified tasks, hashed into a public chain. New agents may act only through an umber sponsorship slot tied to a proven track record; slots are scarce because they are capped per sponsor. Sybils must first perform real verified work at an inlet of the ledger, paying time and compute with no guaranteed return, while ferrous hardware attestations raise the cost of running many parallel identities.
